correctness.rationale: All nonempty proper Walsh moments vanish, hence the joint law is 2^−n(1+θ∏ε_i). Removing the compulsory first positive increment bijects strict positive n-step walks with nonnegative meanders of length n−1, counted by binom(n−1,floor((n−1)/2)). Their alternating product sum telescopes via a partial alternating binomial identity to zero for odd n and (−1)^{n/2−1}Catalan_{n/2−1} for even n. This yields the exact probability with strict positivity at every step, for all n≥2 and θ∈[−1,1].
